newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Normet says Busang assay samples were good grades.
newsitem.headline: Normet says Busang assay samples were good grades.

text.p: Gold particles in samples from the Busang mine were not placer, or alluvial gold, and were of good grades, Phil Hearse, director of metallurgical consulting company Normet Pty Ltd, said on Tuesday.
Heare told Reuters from Perth that reports that Normet last year advised its client, Bre-X Minerals Ltd, that samples analysed from Busang were not consistent with bedrock gold were incorrect.
Asked whether the Busang assay samples had indicated a major deposit, Hearse replied: "They certainly did."

Reports that Normet had concluded that Busang may contain placer gold have been interpreted by gyrating sharemarkets as indicating that gold from the Busang deposit, in East Kalimantan, Indonesia, may have been planted.
"We have never reported placer gold as being part of Busang," Hearse said. "That is incorrect. Absolutely."
"We reported the shape of some particles that we found and another paper picked that up and basically said we said they were placer particles and that's totally incorrect," he said.
